verdict.reasoning: Patient says, “my chest has been feeling really tight” and when asked how long, responds, “Three hours now.”

Patient reports “a little bit short of breath,” feeling “a bit wheezy,” and “kind of cough, coughing.” Doctor summarizes “non-productive cough,” and asks “Is the cough worse at night-time?” Patient: “it gets a little bit worse at night but, basically, just pretty consistent,” supporting mild SOB, wheeze, dry cough, slightly worse at night.

Doctor: “you wouldn't say you've got chest pains? It's more of a tight chest, is it?” Patient: “No, not really pain, it's more like, tight.” When asked “are you coughing up anything?” patient replies, “Uh, no,” indicating no sputum production.

Doctor asks about breathlessness at rest and on exertion. Patient: “I'm definitely not short of breath at rest… It does when I'm walking up stairs, I do feel like, I have a little bit, more short of breath than I would normally be.”

Patient: “I had a cold last week… I had a sore throat, I had a runny nose… Are you feeling better now…? Patient: “the runny nose isn't as bad any more… but the cough's kind of stuck around.” This supports recent URTI with sore throat and rhinorrhea improving, persistent cough.

Patient: “Yeah, yeah, I have asthma, I've had it for a while now.” Regarding severe attack: “when I was in high school, I had to have a tube put down my throat.” When asked age: “I think I was like seventeen. Sixteen maybe.” This indicates severe exacerbation with intubation around 16–17.
Patient: “ohh, when I was young, I also had eczema.”
Patient: “And I had a milk protein allergy, when I was young too.”

Patient: “you know the um, uh, Ventolin. It's called uh, Salbutamol. I got that one,” and doctor later: “you can… use the Clenil Modulite in the morning, with Ventolin as a PRN… when you need to,” supporting PRN use.

Patient: “then I have a steroid, a Clenil, Clenil inhaler.” Later: “I was away at uni last week, and I forgot to bring it with me… they ran out and I… forgot to, go and grab the next one… About a week ago.” Doctor: “you haven't got any Clenil, or any Ventolin at the moment?” Patient: “Not with me right now, no, I ran out.”
Doctor: “any drug allergies, that you know of?” Patient: “No, no, not allergic to anything… nothing, no drugs.”
Patient: “I have like, a hayfever, you know, and some allergies just to dust, stuff like that.”
Patient: “my mum has eczema.”
Patient: “and my dad has asthma.”
Patient: “I was away at uni last week,” which supports that he is a university student.

Doctor states impression: “you've had this cold, so you've got wheezy with a cough,” and discusses this as “this asthma attack,” in the context of not having Clenil or Ventolin for about a week. This supports acute asthma exacerbation likely post-viral and after lapse in preventer/reliever.

Doctor: “I would quite like to… get you some, uh, Ventolin… What I'd like to do is… send you these, the, some prescriptions for your, uh, inhalers… you can… use the Clenil Modulite in the morning, with Ventolin as a PRN… And the other thing I'd like to send you is a spacer.” This supports Salbutamol PRN via spacer.
Doctor: “send you these… prescriptions for your, uh, inhalers, ongoing… once you get better from this asthma attack, you can, you can, use the Clenil Modulite in the morning, with Ventolin as a PRN.”

Doctor: “give you a, dose of steroids. So this is, these are tablets which, um, you can take for five days. Uh, two tablets in the morning… they can make you, your mood change… can give you, a high blood sugar… can also cause rash, nausea, um, headaches,” confirming 5‑day oral steroid course, 2 tablets each morning, with side effects discussed.

Doctor: “the other thing I'd like to send you is a spacer… I'll send you another one, and it has some instructions about how to use it, but essentially, uh, couple of puffs to prime it… breathing in and out… for five or ten breaths.”

Doctor: “If you should start to use the Ventolin more than, uh, every three hours… it's a good idea to seek medical attention.” Also: “Any deterioration in your symptoms, like worsening shortness of breath… or just generally concerning symptoms… then, seek further medical attention anytime please.”
Doctor: “I might give you some time off work as well. You can self-certify first seven days, but uh, I think I would advise you just to, rest a little bit until you're feeling a bit better.”
